Hi Helium D..
I got my B30 this Thursday the 5th of Nov and the hardware build looks solid.
The Glod software is not running very well the miner stops running at random intervals and has yet to run 25h with out needing a reboot to start mining again no matter the power mode.
I was really looking forward to having Harlo OS on it, but from the last 2 streams from JD it sound like he is no longer going to release one.
i have attached the system log from yesterday, it only mined for 4 to 5 hours before stopping again.
Regards
Christian
Searched the web · Harlo OS B30 firmware harlolabs
Handed to the team · Needs JD: (1) the Harlo OS plan for the B30, which I can't confirm and harlolabs

Hi Christian,

Thanks for the detailed write-up, and I'm glad the build looks solid. A miner that needs a reboot every few hours isn't good enough, so let's work out why it stops.

First, the system log didn't come through on our side. Could you reply to this email with it attached again? A .txt or .zip ····best, or you can paste the last part of it from just before it stopped. Please include these details in the same reply:

1. The firmware version shown in the web interface.
2. Which power modes you tried, and the hashrate each one showed. The B30 is rated at 30 TH/s, and any mode that runs it above that counts as overclocking, which the warranty doesn't cover. That's why I need to know what it has been running at.
3. Whether it's on Wi-Fi or Ethernet, and which pool it's pointed at.
4. What it looks like when it stops. Does the web interface still load, with the hashrate at zero or the pool shown as disconnected? Or is the interface unreachable and the screen frozen? Are the fans still spinning?

That last point matters most. It tells us whether the miner is losing its pool connection, hanging in the firmware or dropping out on power or heat.

While you gather that, a few things are worth trying:

1. If you can, use an Ethernet cable instead of Wi-Fi.
2. Add a backup pool in the second pool slot. If the main pool drops, the miner then switches over instead of sitting idle.
3. Plug the B30 straight into a wall outlet, not a power strip or extension cord, on a circuit without other heavy loads.
4. Give it a few inches of clear space around the air intake and exhaust.

About Harlo OS on the B30: I can't confirm what was said on the streams, and I won't guess at the roadmap. The B30 isn't on the list of supported models on our Harlo OS page right now. I've passed your question to JD, our hardware lead, along with the stability problem. The team is offline for the weekend and picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer will come to you by email.

For a faster answer, JD and the community are very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post in the Harlo OS channel and mention @nullhashrate.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Searched the web · esp-idf "transport_base" "Failed to open a new connection"

Hi Christian,

Thanks, that's very useful. The details you gave already narrow it down a lot.

The zip ····'t reach us this time either, so I haven't been able to open the log. Could you paste the text into the body of your reply instead? About 100 lines from just before it stops mining would be ideal.

Here's what the lines you pasted tell me. "transport_base: Failed to open a new connection" isn't a Glod error code. It's a generic network message from the Espressif ESP-IDF framework that runs on the miner's control board. Developer reports on Espressif's GitHub show it right after the underlying connection attempt fails. Common causes are
"connect() error: Host is unreachable"
, a failed hostname lookup (
"couldn't get hostname for :example.com"
) or a
"select() timeout"
. So the miner is trying to open a connection every half second and can't reach what it's aiming at. That fits what you see: the web interface keeps working, the hashboards drop to zero, and it never fails over. What that line doesn't tell us is which connection is failing (pool 1, pool 2 or something else) or why. The one or two lines just above each "transport_base" line usually say whether it's DNS, host unreachable or a timeout, which is why I'd like the pasted text.

I'm not treating this as a hardware fault. The board, temperatures and power are behaving. This is a network or firmware behaviour, so here are three tests worth running:

1. Swap the pools for one run. Put your internal BCH solo pool in slot 1 and pool.harlolabs in slot 2. Your local pool doesn't depend on your internet connection or on DNS. If the B30 then runs past 24 hours, the problem is on the path out to the external pool. If it still stops, that points to the firmware itself.
2. Give the B30 a fixed address on your router (a DHCP reservation), and check that the DNS server the miner uses is one that is always reachable. If the router hands out a new lease or DNS hiccups, a firmware that doesn't recover well can get stuck exactly like this.
3. When it stops next time, before you reboot, take the screenshot you mentioned, note the time and copy the log. With the timestamp we can line it up with your router or pool logs.

The failover is a separate problem. A miner that stops instead of switching to pool 2 is firmware behaviour, and I'll include it in what JD sees. Your firmware identifies itself as "GLOD P6, VER 1.0.0 20261010", and I've noted that too.

Your question about Harlo OS for the B30 and the stability issue are already with JD. Your new details go into the same thread, so he'll see everything together when the team is back tomorrow at 10am ET. His answer will come to your email. The Discord is still the quickest way to reach him: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , mention @nullhashrate in the Harlo OS channel. Posting the pasted log there helps too.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Handed to the team · The diagnosis has shifted from the network to a possible board or sensor fault,

Hi Christian,

Great catch, and thanks for the screenshot. This changes the picture, and I owe you a correction: the network errors I focused on last time are not what stops it. Your log shows it hashing at a steady 23.6 to 24.7 TH/s, with only 16 rejected shares, straight through those "transport_base" lines. They're background noise, not the cause.

Your screenshot shows the actual stop. Both hashboards were cut at the same moment. The dashboard reads Power 0 W, both boards sit at 0.05 V, and the chips have cooled to 19 °C, the same as the VRM. The web interface is still up, Ethernet is connected and both fans are still turning at 20%. The chart shows the hashrate holding at about 25 TH/s until about 9:36 and dropping to zero at 9:37. The line that climbs back and slowly decays after that is the smoothed average running down, not real mining.

The log before the cutoff backs up what you're seeing. Over the 13 hours, the "Power Temp" value stayed between 73 and 79 °C, the board temps between 47 and 54 °C, the current steady at about 50 A and both fans at about 1,900 RPM. Nothing was climbing. A part that reads 77 to 80 °C doesn't really jump to 122 °C between two readings while the load and cooling stay the same. So a bad temperature reading tripping the protection fits better than real overheating. I can't rule out the regulator itself from here, though, and the firmware also isn't recovering on its own after the cutoff. Both are calls for JD, our hardware lead, and I've sent him all of this with your screenshot.

The lines that decide it are the ones from the moment it happened. The text you pasted ends at 05:02, a few hours before the 9:37 cutoff. Next time it stops, please copy the log before you reboot and paste these lines into your reply: the last few SYS_MON readings before the cut, the line that shows the 122 °C reading, and whatever line says the boards were shut off. I also need to know which label the jump is on: "Power Temp", "Board Temp" or a chip temperature. That tells JD whether it's the regulator sensor or the chip sensor.

Running Balanced at about 312 W and 24 TH/s is well within spec, so you don't need to change any settings. Keep it running as it is so we can catch the next stop.

The team is back today at 10am ET, and JD's answer will come to your email. The fastest way to reach him directly is still the Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post the screenshot and the log lines in the Harlo OS channel and mention @nullhashrate.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Handed to the team · New symptom on top of the open hashboard-cutoff issue (flagged Nov 8 and Nov 9).

Hi Christian,

Thanks for the new screenshot. I've gone through it, and you're right about the lower board.

At Balanced with the fans at 40%, it shows 22.1 TH/s in total at 266 W. The upper board (0) makes 12.11 TH/s on 134.5 W, which is 11.1 J/TH. The lower board (1) makes only 9.99 TH/s on 131.6 W, which is 13.2 J/TH. Both boards get the same 3.22 V and run at the same 600 MHz. Both show 3 chips, and both are running cool: chips at 52 and 50 °C, regulators at 53 and 51 °C, VRM at 53 °C, fans at about 3,200 RPM.

So board 1 draws the same power as board 0 but returns about 2 TH/s less. Heat doesn't explain it, because board 1 is actually the cooler one. Settings don't either, because both boards run the same voltage and frequency. Since all chips still show up, it isn't a chip that has dropped out. Taken together with the earlier sudden cutoffs, this looks to me like something JD needs to judge as a possible hardware issue rather than a setting.

To your question: I can't see a reply from JD in this thread yet, and I'm sorry you've had to chase it. I've sent him this new finding together with both screenshots and everything from the earlier cutoffs.

Three things will help him decide:

1. Copy the latest SYS_MON lines from the log and paste them into your reply. They include the "hw" (hardware error) count, and a rising count there would point to the board.
2. If it has cut out again since Monday, paste the lines from that moment: the last readings before the cut, the 122 °C line and the shutdown line.
3. Unplug the unit at the wall for a full minute, let it run for an hour, and tell me whether board 1 comes back level with board 0 or stays about 2 TH/s down.

The team is back tomorrow at 10am ET, and JD's answer will come to your email. The fastest way to reach him directly is the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf . Post both screenshots in the Harlo OS channel and mention @nullhashrate.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
